# Section 030: Controls and Frameworks

Makes the reader able to explain how security controls, risk and frameworks fit together and to enforce a control in a cluster. It covers the words the KCSA (Kubernetes and Cloud Native Security Associate) exam uses: threat, vulnerability, risk, preventive, detective and corrective control, framework, benchmark, evidence, STRIDE and residual risk. It then turns a written rule into an admission control and tests what that control does not cover.

**Exam objective covered:** Controls and Frameworks (Overview of Cloud Native Security, 14% of the exam)

---

## What You Will Master

- Distinguish a threat, a vulnerability, a risk and a security control
- Compare preventive, detective and corrective controls, using the Pod Security Admission modes as an example
- Explain how a framework (NIST CSF, PCI DSS, NIST SSDF, SLSA) differs from a benchmark (CIS Kubernetes Benchmark)
- Collect evidence about the live cluster with kubectl and jq
- Name the six STRIDE categories and choose a risk treatment (mitigate, avoid, transfer, accept)
- Write a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and binding with the Deny, Warn and Audit actions and roll it out in steps
- Test a control with a request that must fail and one that must pass, and name the requests it does not match

---

## The Learning Path

### 1. Controls, Risk And Frameworks
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 1: Controls, Risk And Frameworks](./module-01/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-030/module-01/playground` — kind cluster, no extra tools. The Starfleet workloads in `starfleet` with no Pod Security labels, a privileged `debug-tools` Deployment (on purpose) and `outpost` with the `drifter` client.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS041.git -c sections/section-030/module-01/playground
    ```

### 2. Enforcing Controls With Admission Policy
*   **Module Reader:** **[Module 2: Enforcing Controls With Admission Policy](./module-02/course.md)**
*   **Hands-on Playground:** `sections/section-030/module-02/playground` — kind cluster, no extra tools. The Starfleet workloads in `starfleet`, where `probe` has no memory limit (on purpose), and no admission policy yet.
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS041.git -c sections/section-030/module-02/playground
    ```

### Section Capstone Challenge
*   **Comprehensive Challenge:** Controls And Frameworks Capstone — `sections/section-030/capstone/labs/lab-01`
    ```bash
    astrona run --git ssh://git@github.com/astrona-io/ATS041.git -c sections/section-030/capstone/labs/lab-01
    astrona submit -c .
    ```
*   **Hands-on Objective:** A new team namespace `orbit` must meet a security standard. The reader labels it with Pod Security levels, removes a privileged workload, binds a memory-limit admission policy to `orbit` only, and fixes a Deployment so that it complies. The grader checks the labels, a dry-run rejection, the scope of the binding and that `starfleet` and `outpost` stay unchanged.
